newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 19.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 19.5 percent.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading for the week of September 16-20 averaged 19.5 percent of the exchange's average daily volume of 436.7 million shares, or 85.3 million shares a day.
It said the average included program trading related to the September 20 quarterly expiration of stock-index options and futures.
In the week of September 9-13, trading averaged 8.5 percent of a volume of 388.4 million shares, or 33.2 million shares.
The following week, buy programs accounted for a daily average of 45.9 million shares and sell programs 39.4 million, the exchange said.
In all markets, program trading averaged 107.2 million shares a day the week, 79.5 percent of it on the exchange, 10.4 percent in other domestic markets and the remaining 10.1 percent abroad.

The exchange said the five most active member firms were Moruma Securities, Morgan Stanley, Salomon Brothers, First Option and Susquehanna Brokerage Services. Nomura executed most of its program activity for its own account, while the others executed all or most of their program activity for customers, it said.
During the week, 36.0 percent of program volume executed by the exchange member firms related to index arbitrage. Another 7.7 percent involved derivative product-related strategies.
All other types of portfolio trading strategies combined accounted for 56.3 percent of member firms' program trading volume during the week.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
